definition: Mihaela van der Schaar is the John Humphrey Plummer Professor of Machine Learning, AI, and Medicine at the University of Cambridge, where she is director of the Cambridge Centre for AI in Medicine (CCAIM), and a Chancellor's Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the University of California, Los Angeles.
details: Her research involves topics in signal and image processing, communication networks, network science, multimedia, game theory, distributed systems, machine learning, and AI. van der Schaar focuses on medical applications of computer engineering, including AI-enabled personalized medicine.

explainer.lead: Mihaela van der Schaar is the John Humphrey Plummer Professor of Machine Learning, AI, and Medicine at the University of Cambridge, where she directs the Cambridge Centre for AI in Medicine (CCAIM); she is also a Chancellor's Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UCLA. Her focus on AI-enabled personalized medicine places her among the researchers shaping how machine learning is applied to clinical care.

tiers.eli5: She is a professor who leads a Cambridge centre where computers are taught to help doctors give each patient care tailored to them.
tiers.practitioner: Her work spans signal and image processing, communication networks, network science, multimedia, game theory, distributed systems, machine learning and AI. Engineers working on health data should note that her work is framed around medical applications, not general-purpose model design.
tiers.paperLevel: She holds the John Humphrey Plummer Professorship of Machine Learning, AI, and Medicine at the University of Cambridge and a Chancellor's Professorship of Electrical and Computer Engineering at UCLA; her research topics are listed as signal and image processing, communication networks, network science, multimedia, game theory, distributed systems, machine learning, and AI, concentrated on AI-enabled personalized medicine.

explainer.example: A team building a personalized treatment model would look to her centre's work on medical applications of machine learning, where the emphasis is on AI-enabled personalized medicine.
